region.label: SECTION 1.01 - Applicable Liquidity Threshold / Applicable Rate

operativeSourceText:
“Applicable Liquidity Threshold” means $37.5 million; provided
that to the extent that, as of any date of determination, the maximum committed amount of the Super-Senior Revolving Facility (or any Refinancing Indebtedness in respect thereof) is increased in excess of $62.0 million (such excess amount, the
“RCF Increase Amount”), the Applicable Liquidity Threshold shall be increased by an amount equal to 26.0% of the RCF Increase Amount up to a maximum Applicable Liquidity Threshold not to exceed $50.0 million.

“Applicable Rate” means a percentage per annum equal to (i) until delivery of the financial statements for the first
full fiscal quarter ending after the Closing Date pursuant to Section 6.01, (A) 8.00% for Term Benchmark Loans, and (B) 7.00% for Base Rate Loans and (ii) thereafter, the following percentages per annum, based upon the Secured Net Leverage

Any increase or decrease in the Applicable Rate resulting from a change in the Secured Net Leverage Ratio
shall become effective as of the first Business Day immediately following the date a Compliance Certificate is delivered pursuant to Section 6.02(1); provided that, at the option of the Required Facility Lenders, “Pricing
Level 1” (as set forth above) shall apply as of (x) the first Business Day after the date on which a Compliance Certificate was required to have been delivered but was not delivered, and shall continue to so apply to and including the
date on which such Compliance Certificate is so delivered (and thereafter the pricing level otherwise determined in accordance with this definition shall apply) or (y) the first Business Day after an Event of Default under Section 8.01(1)
shall have occurred and be continuing, and shall continue to so apply to but excluding the date on which such Event of Default is cured or waived (and thereafter the pricing level otherwise determined in accordance with this definition shall apply).

“Appropriate Lender” means, at any time, with respect to Loans of any Class, the Lenders of such Class.

“Approved Fund” means, with respect to any Lender, any Fund that is administered, advised or managed by (a) such Lender,
(b) an Affiliate of such Lender or (c) an entity or an Affiliate of an entity that administers, advises or manages such Lender.

“Asset Sale” means:

(1) the sale, conveyance, transfer or other disposition, whether in a single transaction or a series of related transactions of
property or assets of the Borrower or any Subsidiary of the Borrower (each referred to in this definition as a “disposition”); or

(2) the issuance or sale of Equity Interests (other than Preferred Stock or Disqualified Stock of Subsidiaries issued in
compliance with Section 7.02 and directors’ qualifying shares or shares or interests required to be held by foreign nationals or other third parties to the extent required by applicable Law) of any Subsidiary (other than to the Borrower or
another Subsidiary), whether in a single transaction or a series of related transactions;

irExtensionCandidates.sourceEvidence: §1.01, Applicable Rate: '(A) 8.00% for Term Benchmark Loans, and (B) 7.00% for Base Rate Loans' and the pricing grid's two parallel columns (Term Benchmark / Base Rate)
irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: A way to select between parallel rate/value tracks keyed by a non-numeric categorical attribute of the transaction (here, Loan Type: Term Benchmark vs. Base Rate), analogous to a CASE/enum-equality test.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: COMPARE requires both operands to be the same literal type (MONEY/NUMBER/RATIO/DATE/BOOLEAN) and there is no STRING/ENUM literal kind, so a genuine equality test against a category like 'Loan Type = Term Benchmark' cannot be expressed with COMPARE. IF's condition must therefore be approximated with a TRANSACTION_INPUT_REFERENCE treated as an implicit boolean, which loses the enumerated-category semantics and the fact that there may be more than two mutually exclusive categories (e.g., additional Classes).
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: A CATEGORY_MATCH/ENUM_EQUALS node (inputName, matchValue, possibleValues) usable directly as a boolean-valued condition in IF/AND/OR/NOT, to formally encode enumerated-category selection (Loan Type, Class, etc.) distinct from a generic transaction input.

This submission covers the definitions found within the supplied §1.01 excerpt: Applicable Liquidity Threshold, Applicable Rate, Appropriate Lender, Approved Fund, and Asset Sale. No independently operative WireRules (permissions/prohibitions) arise from this text itself - it is a defined-terms section; the terms are consumed elsewhere in the Agreement by rules not part of this submission.

Cross-referenced regions in Sections 10.07, 6.01, 6.02(1) and 8.01(1) were used only to confirm the meaning of cross-references made by the definitions being compiled (e.g., what 'Section 6.01' delivery means, what 'Event of Default under Section 8.01(1)' means) - their own internal thresholds (e.g., $1.0mm minimum assignment amount, $3,500 processing fee, 90/45-day financial statement deadlines) are economics of those OTHER sections, not of this provision, and were intentionally left un-consumed as genuinely non-operative to this compilation.

For Asset Sale exceptions (b), (c) and (r), getReferencedProvision was affirmatively used to attempt resolution of Sections 7.03, 7.05 and 7.01 respectively; each returned only general prohibition/heading-level text rather than the specific enumerated permitted-exception lists those Asset Sale carve-outs incorporate by reference (including the Section 7.03(6)/(7) carve-back). irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: COMPARE requires both operands to be the same literal type (MONEY/NUMBER/RATIO/DATE/BOOLEAN) and there is no STRING/ENUM literal kind, so a genuine equality test against a category like 'Loan Type = Term Benchmark' cannot be expressed with COMPARE. IF's condition must therefore be approximated with a TRANSACTION_INPUT_REFERENCE treated as an implicit boolean, which loses the enumerated-category semantics and the fact that there may be more than two mutually exclusive categories (e.g., additional Classes).

No independently operative WireRules (permissions/prohibitions) arise from this text itself - it is a defined-terms section; the terms are consumed elsewhere in the Agreement by rules not part of this submission.

Cross-referenced regions in Sections 10.07, 6.01, 6.02(1) and 8.01(1) were used only to confirm the meaning of cross-references made by the definitions being compiled (e.g., what 'Section 6.01' delivery means, what 'Event of Default under Section 8.01(1)' means) - their own internal thresholds (e.g., $1.0mm minimum assignment amount, $3,500 processing fee, 90/45-day financial statement deadlines) are economics of those OTHER sections, not of this provision, and were intentionally left un-consumed as genuinely non-operative to this compilation.

For Asset Sale exceptions (b), (c) and (r), getReferencedProvision was affirmatively used to attempt resolution of Sections 7.03, 7.05 and 7.01 respectively; each returned only general prohibition/heading-level text rather than the specific enumerated permitted-exception lists those Asset Sale carve-outs incorporate by reference (including the Section 7.03(6)/(7) carve-back). These remain MISSING_CONTEXT at the specific-branch level, reflected in the Asset Sale definition's PARTIAL sufficiency and reasons.

Several context-bundle items for terms outside this provision's own text (e.g., 'Benchmark', 'Floor', 'Benchmark Replacement', 'NYFRB Rate') were flagged AMBIGUOUS_TARGET/collision in Phase 2 context; none of those terms were required to represent the five definitions compiled here, so they were not relied upon.

findings.verifierReasoning: The source fully specifies a computable interest-rate definition: two flat initial rates and a three-tier leverage-based grid, plus a lender-election override mechanism tied to late Compliance Certificates or a continuing Event of Default under Section 8.01(1). Nearly all of this is unambiguous (the only genuine ambiguity is the exact-boundary gap at ratio = 1.00x/0.50x, which the compiler correctly flagged separately). Despite this, the proposed IR's actual calculationExpression resolves, at its very root, to kind "UNSUPPORTED" - meaning the compiled/reachable IR delivers literally no computable Applicable Rate value at all. The correct-looking percentages and thresholds exist only inside an "attemptedStructure" field that is explicitly non-operative debug content (this is corroborated by the deterministic pass, which could not find any of the 0.08/0.07/0.0775/0.0675/0.075/0.065 PERCENT values or the 1/0.5 RATIO values anywhere in the compiled IR, even though they are literally present in the JSON text). The root cause appears to be that several boolean conditions (e.g., "Loan Type is Term Benchmark Loan", "Determination date precedes delivery of financial statements...") were tagged with type "MONEY" instead of "BOOLEAN", causing a type-check cascade failure up the entire tree. The definition's own sufficiency is marked "PARTIAL", which materially understates the actual gap - a reviewer relying on "PARTIAL" would reasonably assume some portion of the rate is computable, when in fact zero percent of it is. This is one of the most economically significant terms in the credit agreement (it sets the borrower's actual interest cost), so a confidently-mislabeled complete failure here is a material discrepancy a reviewer must be alerted to.
